T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.

T1110.003.name: Password Spraying
T1110.003.description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining access.

T1046.name: Network Service Scanning
T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure.

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

T1566.name: Phishing
T1566.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

T1078.004.name: Cloud Accounts
T1078.004.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a cloud account to gain access.

T1556.name: Modify Authentication Process
T1556.description: Adversaries may modify authentication mechanisms and processes to access user credentials.

T1204.name: User Execution
T1204.description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol
T1071.description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering.
